turns.question: Under which circumstances can a concern or complaint be made under this University of Essex whistleblowing policy?
turns.retrieval_query: Under which circumstances can a concern or complaint be made under this University of Essex whistleblowing policy?
turns.answer:
Concerns or disclosures that are in the public interest, meaning they are disclosures of serious wrongdoing that have an impact beyond the individual making the disclosure, can be raised under the Whistleblowing Policy. These concerns must also be made in accordance with the procedures and in the reasonable belief that it tends to show malpractice and is in the public interest. Concerns that are solely of a personal nature should be raised under the Code of Student Conduct or the Student Concerns and Complaints Procedure. [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf]

Sources:
*   [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf)

turns.question: Who can someone raise that concern with?
turns.retrieval_query: Who can someone raise a concern with under the University of Essex whistleblowing policy?
turns.answer: Concerns should be raised in the first instance with your line manager or formally with the University Secretary. [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf]

turns.question: What constitutes plagiarism according to the academic offences procedure?
turns.retrieval_query: What constitutes plagiarism according to the University of Essex academic offences procedure?
turns.answer: According to the academic offences procedures, plagiarism is using or copying the work of others (whether written, printed, or in any other form) without proper acknowledgment in any assignment, examination, or other assessed work. [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedures-2017-18.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedures-2017-18.pdf) and [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedure.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedure.pdf).

turns.question: What penalties can be applied for that?
turns.retrieval_query: What penalties can be applied for plagiarism according to the academic offences procedure?
turns.answer:
Here's a breakdown of potential penalties, referencing both the 2017-18 and 2025-26 procedures:

**For Postgraduate Research Students (2017-18):**

*   **Prior to submission:** Penalty 1: Formal written warning. Penalty 2: Specified section must be corrected/rewritten & resubmitted. Penalty 3: No longer eligible for full award; downgrade and consider a lesser award. Penalty 4: Required to withdraw with no qualification awarded. [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedures-2017-18.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedures-2017-18.pdf)
*   **After submission:** Penalty 1: Formal written warning. Penalty 2: Examiners consider non-plagiarized sections for the degree. [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedures-2017-18.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedures-2017-18.pdf)

**For Undergraduate and Postgraduate Taught Students (2025-26):**

*   Penalty 1: Formal written warning only
*   Penalty 2: Resubmit unit with minor amendments for an uncapped mark
*   Penalty 3a: Resubmit unit with minor amendments for a capped mark
*   Penalty 3b: Resubmit dissertation (Postgraduate Taught) with amendments for a capped mark.
*   Penalty 4: Mark of zero, reassessment available
*   Penalty 5: Mark of zero, no reassessment
*   Penalty 6: Mark of zero, no resubmission or reassessment
*   Penalty 7: No longer eligible for full award. [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedure.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/academic-offences-procedure.pdf)

Sources:

turns.question: What does the Fitness to Study policy address in terms of student behavior?
turns.retrieval_query: What does the Fitness to Study policy address in terms of student behavior?
turns.answer: The Fitness to Study policy addresses situations where a student’s health, mental health, or behaviour is causing concern. This includes behavior within accommodation that causes difficulties for other students or staff, and when a student's behavior impacts adversely on others around them, including suicidal or self-harming behaviors. The University may terminate a student’s accommodation contract if their behavior poses a risk to themselves or others. [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/fitness-to-study.pdf]

turns.answer: A "Capped Mark" means that when reassessment is offered for a capped Module Mark, the maximum mark recorded for the Module Aggregate is 40. The actual mark achieved will be used to determine if the assessment has been passed and will appear on your transcript. [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/ug/current/glossary/roa-ug-glossary.pdf]

turns.question: Going back to my earlier question about student behavior concerns - who initiates that process?
turns.retrieval_query: Who initiates the process for addressing student behavior concerns under the Fitness to Study policy?
turns.answer: If a student’s behavior or wellbeing is causing ongoing concern, but not presenting an immediate crisis, the process should begin by approaching the student and discussing those concerns directly. Guidance can be sought from the Student Wellbeing and Inclusivity Service to determine who should approach the student and how best to do so. Ideally, this would be a staff member who knows the student, such as their Accessibility and Wellbeing or Wellbeing Adviser (if they have one), personal tutor, or another departmental staff member. [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/fitness-to-study.pdf]

This applies to both the MSc Periodontology programme [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/mscperiodontology_25.pdf] and the Postgraduate Diploma in Periodontology [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/pg_dip_periodontology_25.pdf].

turns.question: What happens if a student exceeds that trailing credit limit?
turns.retrieval_query: What happens if a student exceeds the trailing credit limit of 30 credits for both the MSc Periodontology programme and the Postgraduate Diploma in Periodontology?
turns.answer: If a student exceeds the 30-credit trailing limit, an in-year Board of Examiners meeting may be convened [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/pg_dip_periodontology_25.pdf]. The board will either withdraw the student or, if extenuating circumstances are accepted, may offer additional assessment opportunities [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/pg_dip_periodontology_25.pdf].

turns.question: Switching topics - what's the minimum pass mark for all modules in East 15 Acting School's Masters programmes?
turns.retrieval_query: What is the minimum pass mark for all modules in East 15 Acting School's Masters programmes?
turns.answer: The pass mark for all modules in East 15 Acting School’s Masters programmes is 50 [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/east15-25.pdf].

turns.question: Back to the very first thing I asked about the credit limit - which department administers that programme?
turns.retrieval_query: Which department administers the MSc Periodontology and Postgraduate Diploma in Periodontology programmes?
turns.answer:
The 30-credit trailing limit applies to programmes administered by the Health and Social Care department [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/mscperiodontology_25.pdf] [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/pg_dip_periodontology_25.pdf].
